requirement:
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
rationale:
The subject has three obligations. I found tests for each.

1. Existing evidence's inputs, determination and rationale MUST NOT enter the mandatory input set.
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` writes old evidence with `notes.txt` (which exists), a false determination and the rationale "old secret judgment". It asserts that `recorded_inputs()` is empty, that no input has `file == notes.txt`, and that the serialized inputs omit the old rationale.
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[earlier_evidence_inputs_and_judgments_are_not_carried_forward]` records the old evidence file itself and `notes.txt` as earlier inputs. It asserts that neither `notes.txt`, `evidence/` nor the old rationale appears in the supplied inputs. It also asserts that the evidence file on disk is unchanged.

2. The same content MUST NOT be supplied to the model.
   - `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reassessment_records_only_freshly_delivered_inputs]` runs a full `assess` against a recording provider. It asserts that the first prompt does not contain `deleted.rs`, `fn[old]` or `OLD_RATIONALE`.

3. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs supplied to it. Sources that no longer exist or are no longer relevant MUST NOT block or shape reassessment.
   - `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reassessment_records_only_freshly_delivered_inputs]` asserts that the new record contains the fresh `requirements.ready` input and none of the stale strings. It also asserts that the rationale is "Fresh assessment."
   - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` records three earlier inputs that no longer resolve: a missing file, a removed Rust item and a removed requirement. It asserts that `prepare` succeeds and that the mandatory inputs are exactly the subject's own declaration.

The positive clause, that existing evidence only determines whether a subject needs assessment, is carried out by the staleness and skip logic in `src/authoring/batch.rs`. Other requirements, such as `requirements.authoring.reassessment`, govern that logic. The subject's own negative obligations are checked in both the input-bundle tests and the end-to-end test.

I found no input class that the text names and these tests miss.
